Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
133 PM EDT Thu Sep 17 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 314 AM EDT Thursday...

No significant changes.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 314 AM EDT Thursday...

1. Light rain showers will move across our area today, 
especially our southern Vermont zones. Drier breezy conditions 
return on Friday with cool temperatures overnight.

2. Next chance for showers will be early Sunday, also 
especially our southern Vermont zones. 

3. From Monday through Wednesday dry weather is likely along 
with a warming trend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 314 AM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: An open wave of low pressure passes south of our
forecast area today, spreading some light rain showers across 
the region. Best chance for showers in our area will be across 
southern Vermont, but have some mention of showers across areas 
as far north as the international border. Maximum temperatures 
today will range through the 70s. Rainfall totals will be up to 
four tenths of an inch in our extreme southern zones, with many 
areas not measuring. A ridge of surface high pressure will then 
build into our area from the north on Friday into Friday night. 
This will bring drier weather, and some gusty winds on Friday 
followed by cool temperatures Friday night with ideal 
radiational cooling conditions in place.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Another low pressure system will pass south of 
our area Saturday night into Sunday, once again our best chances
for showers will be across our southern zones. Models are 
finally starting to fall into better agreement with how far 
north the precipitation will spread. Precipitation will be more 
widespread with this system than the previous one. At this time 
around a tenth of an inch of rain along the international border
up to three quarters of an inch in southern Vermont can be 
expected.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Our region should be under the influence of a 
seasonably cool high pressure area gradually moving eastward to 
start the work week. Temperatures should be about 10 degrees 
below normal Monday trending to around normal on Wednesday. With
this pattern and 925 millibar temperatures falling to near the 
10th percentile, Tuesday morning should be another frosty one 
for sheltered areas that already saw frost Saturday morning. 

An expansive ridge over southern Quebec with the upper level 
ridge axis centered farther west will tend to keep our air quite
dry through this period, with both temperatures and dew points 
gradually modifying. Somewhat increasing spread in guidance with
regards to the position of a slow moving trough to our south, 
and associated increases in moisture, is evident. As such, 
slight chances of rain do come farther north/east at times 
Tuesday and Wednesday, possibly reaching our region. For now, 
the consensus strongly favors rainfree conditions (PoPs 15% or 
less) even if cloud cover tends to increase.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 18Z Friday...Mostly VFR conditions currently across our
taf sites with just a few intervals of IFR cigs at MPV/EFK
through early this aftn. Radar imagery is showing rain showers
angling toward RUT terminal in the next 1 to 2 hours, which will
produce MVFR with some IFR conditions possible toward sunset.
Also, as moisture increases additional MVFR cigs are likely
(60%) at MPV/EFK/SLK and BTV, while VFR prevails at PBG/MSS. 
Later this evening expect the highest probability (60-70%) of 
IFR or lower conditions will at RUT/MPV/SLK by midnight with 
chance probability (25-35%) of IFR cigs or vis possible at 
BTV/MSS and EFK. Did note very warm sfc dwpts in the upper 50s 
to mid 60s this aftn, which would support fog development 
overnight, but sounding data shows increasing bl winds from the 
northwest after 06z at 4 to 8 knots with favorable mixing under 
modest low level caa, which could offset fog development. A mix 
of IFR cigs/vis are possible, given the setup, especially at
RUT.
